scenarios.name: drive_tracking_command
scenarios.description: Healthy drive: commanded to 60%, running at 58%. A 2-point offset is inside the 5% tolerance and the drive is well above the evaluation floor, so the rule is live and silent.

scenarios.name: feedback_below_command
scenarios.description: Commanded to 60%, running at 40%: the drive is 20 points short of what it was asked for. Both delays run from t=0 under delayOnInit, so the alarm lands 600 s in (deviation_duration + alarm_delay).

scenarios.name: feedback_above_command
scenarios.description: The mirror case: commanded to 40%, running at 60%. Abs makes the test symmetric, so a drive overrunning its command alarms exactly as a drive falling short does.

scenarios.name: deviation_exactly_at_threshold
scenarios.description: Boundary: 60% commanded against 55% feedback is a deviation of exactly speed_error_threshold (5.0). CDL Reals has no GreaterEqual, so the comparison is strict and exactly 5 clears.

scenarios.name: deviation_just_above_threshold
scenarios.description: Boundary from the other side: 54.9% feedback against the same command is a 5.1-point deviation, and the alarm lands after the two delays.

scenarios.name: command_below_run_floor
scenarios.description: Commanded to 10% — below the drive's own minimum speed — with the drive stopped. The 10-point deviation clears the threshold, but a drive is not obliged to track a command below its minimum, so yCmdOk is false and the verdict is NO_EVAL rather than a fault.

scenarios.name: command_exactly_at_run_floor
scenarios.description: Evaluability boundary: the command sits exactly on min_cmd_for_eval (20.0%). Strict `>` again, so exactly 20 is not evaluable.

scenarios.name: command_just_above_run_floor
scenarios.description: Evaluability boundary from the other side: 20.1% commanded with the drive stopped. The rule becomes evaluable and the standing 20.1-point deviation alarms after the two delays.

scenarios.name: deviation_shorter_than_both_delays
scenarios.description: An 8-minute deviation: long enough to mature `track` (5 min) but only 3 of the further 5 minutes `persist` needs. No alarm. With a single 300 s delay in place of the chain this scenario would fire at 300 s, which is what makes it the regression test for the two-delay structure.

scenarios.name: drive_recovers_after_alarm
scenarios.description: Recovery: the alarm asserts at 600 s and the drive comes back to within 1 point of its command at t=1200 s. Both delays drop on that tick — TrueDelay only delays the rising edge.

scenarios.name: command_drops_below_floor_after_alarm
scenarios.description: The evaluability release: a deviating drive alarms at 600 s, then the loop backs the command down to 10% at t=1200 s. yCmdOk goes false and yFault follows — the host must read that pair as NO_EVAL, not as a drive that fixed itself.
